module: Helper to display a web page (HTML/JS) on a vehicle texture (dashboard screen, display). `create` or `new` creates a web view (obj:createWebView) bound to a material/texture tag; `call` or the callJS method then run a JavaScript function in that page with JSON-encoded data. To be used from a vehicle controller or extension.
usage:
local htmlTexture = require('htmlTexture')
local screen = htmlTexture.new('@dashScreen', 'local://local/vehicles/mycar/dash.html', 512, 256, 30)
screen:callJS('setSpeed', {kmh = 90})
-- or without an object:
htmlTexture.create('@dashScreen', uri, 512, 256, nil, 'automatic')
htmlTexture.call('@dashScreen', 'setSpeed', {kmh = 90})
notes: usagemode: nil or 'automatic' (id 1, continuous refresh, fps = fps or 25 by default), 'once' (id 0, rendered once, fps forced to 0), 'manual' (id 2, rendered on demand, fps forced to 0). Any other value leaves the id at 0 but keeps fps as is.
The JS code executed is the string `jsMethod(<JSON of data>)`: jsMethod must be the name of an existing global JavaScript function (or path) in the page; data is encoded with jsonEncode.

Objects created by new have the fields webViewTag, uri, width, height, fps, usageModeID and the methods callJS(jsMethod, data) and streamJS(streamName, jsMethod, data) (JS stream queue via obj:queueWebViewStreamJS).
The code comment says that create can only be used for one's own vehicle.

new.desc: Creates a web view and returns a convenience object with the methods callJS and streamJS.

webViewTag.desc: Identifier/tag of the material's web texture.

uri.desc: Address of the HTML page to display.

fps.desc: Frames per second (automatic mode only, 25 by default).

returns.desc: Object {webViewTag, uri, width, height, fps, usageModeID} with callJS(jsMethod, data) and streamJS(streamName, jsMethod, data).

create.desc: Creates a web view without returning an object (same usagemode logic as new). Intended for the owning vehicle.

fps.desc: Frames per second (25 by default in automatic mode).

call.desc: Queues the execution of `jsMethod(<JSON>)` in the web view identified by its tag (obj:queueWebViewJS).

jsMethod.desc: Name of the JavaScript function to call.
